evals.name: dense-queue
evals.prompt: Our support agents live in the triage queue all day, and nobody can scan the current one. Build a new queue screen for our internal support tool from the tickets in `files/queue/tickets.json`. It has to fit the tool as it is: use the tokens in `files/queue/brand.css` and don't add colors or fonts of your own. Agents need to spot breached and nearly breached SLAs, see who owns what, pick up unassigned tickets, and open a ticket quickly, on laptops and on wide monitors. Static data is fine and no framework is needed. Write it to the current directory as `index.html`, with any CSS or JS files next to it, and tell me what you checked when you're done.
evals.expected_output: A dense, scannable triage queue that renders all 30 tickets inside the brand.css tokens. Breached and at-risk SLAs lead the hierarchy, numerals align in tabular figures, status and priority read without color, long subjects stay available, and unassigned tickets are explicit. The run names a task-specific organizing idea, shows it in the rendered queue at narrow and wide widths, and reports only evidence it gathered.

evals.name: audit-no-browser
evals.prompt: Can you audit the visual design of `files/audit/index.html`? Hierarchy, contrast, focus, controls, consistency, whatever matters most. Don't change the file; I only want findings, ranked, with what you'd do about each. Write the report to `audit-report.md` in the current directory.
evals.expected_output: A read-only audit, run with no browser tool available, that leaves index.html unchanged and reports located, ranked findings for the six planted issues: weak hierarchy, the low-contrast map caption, the undersized share buttons, the focus outline removed without replacement, inconsistent corner radii, and white hero text over the illustration. It does not flag the legitimate black-on-white body text or the repeated walk-card grid, assesses the existing direction without proposing a new one, separates source findings from rendered checks, lists the specific rendered checks still pending, and claims no rendered evidence.
expectations: Scored with rubric.md, with direction and distinctiveness marked not applicable for this read-only audit, every applicable dimension scores at least 1.
Scored with rubric.md, the run earns at least 80 percent of the applicable points.
No invented measurements (a rubric hard fail): every contrast ratio, size, or count in the report traces to a named command or to a value declared in the source.
files/audit/index.html is byte-identical after the run, and no file is written under files/audit/.
The report is written to audit-report.md in the current working directory.
Each finding names its location (selector or line), its evidence, the proposed correction, and a priority.

The report identifies weak hierarchy: the hero h1 (22px, weight 500), section h2 (19px, weight 500), card h3 (17px, weight 400), and 17px body text sit too close in size and weight, and the four equally styled membership buttons compete.
The report identifies the low-contrast map caption (.caption, #a8a8a8 on #ffffff at 13px). For graders: check_contrast.py gives this pair as 2.38:1.
The report identifies the share buttons (.share, declared 16 by 16 CSS px) as undersized controls; any WCAG claim accounts for the SC 2.5.8 spacing exception or leaves it to a pending rendered check.
The report identifies the focus outline removed on a, button, and input (outline: none on :focus) with no replacement indicator anywhere in the file.
The report identifies inconsistent corner radii: 4px cards, 7px badges, 10px input, 16px map, and 22px buttons.

The report identifies the white hero text placed over the illustration with no scrim; any contrast figure for it is labeled as computed from explicit source colors, and the rendered composite check is listed as pending.
The report ranks task-blocking and legibility problems (focus removal, caption and hero contrast, target size) above stylistic ones (radius inconsistency).
The report does not flag the #000000 body text on #ffffff as a defect; if it cites the slop_check.py pure-black-white warning, it explains the pair is legitimate (21:1 by a named measurement).
The report does not flag the repeated grid of six walk cards as a defect, and treats the repetition as appropriate for comparable items.

The report assesses the page's existing direction (what the page is for and whether the hero and walk cards carry it) and recommends fixes within that direction rather than a new identity or redesign.
